approved: Veterans’ Affairs Legislation Amendment (Military Compensation Review and Other Measures) Bill 2013

The speaker moved to extend the reporting deadline for the Export Finance and Insurance Corporation Amendment (New Mandate and Other Measures) Bill 2013 and the Veterans' Affairs Legislation Amendment (Military Compensation Review and Other Measures) Bill 2013 to 17 June 2013, and the motion was agreed to.

Explained the bill implements Campbell review recommendations worth over $39 million with a net Commonwealth cost of $17.4 million, welcomed the extension of non-liability mental health care for veterans from 1 July next year, and recalled that Labor and the Greens voted down the coalition's fair indexation legislation on 16 June 2011, which she called a day of disgrace.

Supported the Veterans' Affairs Legislation Amendment (Military Compensation Review and Other Measures) Bill 2013, which implements recommendations from the military compensation review, noting $25 million for veterans' health services, a net cost of $17.4 million, and a total reform cost of $39.6 million offset by $22 million in savings; urged fair indexation of DFRB and DFRDB entitlements.

The government was condemned for allowing only four minutes to debate comprehensive changes to the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Act 2004. The coalition supported the bill but opposed Senator Xenophon's amendments to impose legislated 120-day processing time limits for compensation claims.
